items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1's default suffocation rule is Properties.<init> indy#6 -> lambda$new$5 = blocksMotion() && isCollisionShapeFullBlock() — NO tag. The port's default is TaggedFullCollision (horizon-world/src/suffocation.rs:72) gated on #causes_suffocation, a tag absent from 26.1 jar data (0 entries) and from prepared block-tags.json (248 tags; jar set == prepared set modulo 4 mineable/* renames). motion.rs:139 requires it via tag(...)?, which errors on missing tags; TagDefinitions::build synthesizes nothing. The startup path resource_load.rs load_resources -> load_core (151) -> gameplay_tables (291) -> MotionResources::load_with_facts (324) propagates the error with motion? — the 26.1 client cannot load its core tables with prepared 26.1 data. The first failure in evaluation order is actually #suppresses_bounce (motion.rs:138, also absent; 1.21.7 hardcodes {minecraft:honey_block} for it at motion.rs:144), then #causes_suffocation. Even if load passed, no default block would suffocate. Contrast: 26.2's motion.rs:65 documents the tag as absent in 26.2 data and uses blocks_motion + MotionFullCollision. CI crate tests do not catch this: data-dependent tests skip quietly without .local. NEW in 26.1 — a template-level 26.3-form leak.
items.title: Default suffocation tag-gated on absent #causes_suffocation — client cannot load core tables

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 rewardTradeXp does NOT level up on trade: it sets updateMerchantTimer = 40 and increaseProfessionLevelOnUpdate = true (pop += 5). customServerAiStep decrements the timer ONLY while not trading (isTrading gate); at 0 it calls increaseMerchantCareer (level+1 + updateTrades) — with NO updateSpecialPrices call, so new offers carry specialPriceDiff 0 until the next session. The 26.1 port levels up IMMEDIATELY in Trader::notify_trade (merchant.rs:399-407) and recomputes special prices for ALL offers including the new ones, with the session-start reputation/hero. Observable: newly-unlocked trades show discounted prices mid-session in the port (full price in vanilla), and the level-up appears at once instead of ~2s after trading ends. The 26.2 port has the correct deferred form (level_up_pending, merchant.rs:413 + trading.rs:333) — the 26.1 port diverged from it. No level_up_pending / update_merchant_timer exists anywhere in the 26.1 port. NEW.
items.title: Villager level-up is immediate and new offers are discounted

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 NewMinecartBehavior.getMaxSpeed = MAX_MINECART_SPEED * (inWater ? 0.5 : 1.0) / 20.0 (rule default 8, min 1, max 1000; the port's formula in max_speed_new (991-994) matches). But AbstractMinecart.getMaxSpeed delegates to the behavior, and MinecartFurnace.getMaxSpeed multiplies the result by 0.75 (wet) / 0.5 (dry) under EITHER behavior. Vanilla calls the VIRTUAL (furnace applies) in calculateTrackSpeed (NewMinecartBehavior:1159) and AbstractMinecart.comeOffTrack (AbstractMinecart:698), but the behavior's OWN getMaxSpeed (no furnace) in moveAlongTrack's step cap (1020). The port uses max_speed_new (no furnace factor) at ALL three sites: step cap (1069 — correct), calculateTrackSpeed cap (1208 — wrong) and comeOffTrack (1344 — wrong). In a minecart_improvements world a furnace minecart is capped at 0.4 dry / 0.2 wet instead of 0.2 / 0.15. Experiment-gated: 26.1 DEFAULT_FLAGS = VANILLA_SET only, so the default (old-behavior) path is correct. The 26.2 port has identical code at all three sites. NEW.
items.title: Furnace minecart too fast under minecart_improvements

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 checks the partner is NOT PANICKING in both places: getFreePartner skips panicking candidates, and canContinueToUse is partner.isAlive() && partner.isInLove() && loveTime < 60 && !partner.isPanicking(). The port's partner search and can_continue omit the panic clause entirely (the Seen struct carries no panicking field). Panic does not clear in-love in either implementation (the port clears in_love only on age != 0 / countdown, ai.rs:1593), so the gap is observable: hit one of two in-love animals and the other keeps following it in the port; vanilla stops. Shared with the 26.2 port's identical code (26.2's sweep passed B3 with it). NEW.
items.title: BreedGoal ignores partner panic

systemic_note: One systemic thread dominates 26.1's Batch 3: 26.3-form leakage — the port was written against 26.3 APIs, tags and data forms that 26.1 lacks, and the failures cluster where 26.1's form differs from 26.3's. The sharpest instance is B3-G22 (the #causes_suffocation tag gate, a startup blocker; #suppresses_bounce fails first). The oracle groups are the same thread on the test side: all 52 failing oracles reference 26.3-only APIs (EntityTypes holder, densityfunction package, record-form packets, 9-arg LocalPlayer, abstract Level.fuelValues, 26.3 tag fields) — mechanical repairs, not port defects. The 1.21.7 batch's three systemic threads resolve unevenly for 26.1: (1) tag/form leakage PERSISTS in a new form — 26.1 is a 26.x version but an EARLY one, so the 26.3 tags/data forms the port carries (G22, G18's predicate form) do not exist in 26.1, while the 1.21.7-era literals (G03 immune blocks) do; (2) goal-cadence conversion is resolved — 26.1 vanilla HAS reducedTickDelay/adjustedTickDelay, so the port's reduced() is correct here (G17); (3) RNG-stream divergences are mostly resolved — G13 fixed (unconditional draw), G02's form is vanilla's; only G11's y-range bound remains, a single-site off-by-one, plus the finalize draw-order note (values correct, streams diverge). The remaining port gaps are independent single-site omissions (G04, G05/G27/G28, G06, G09, G23, G24, G25, G26), eight of them carried over from 1.21.7 and seven new or newly found in 26.1 — and three of the new ones (food table, BreedGoal panic, furnace cap) are shared verbatim with the 26.2 port, which passed those sections, so the 26.2 record needs the same flags.
